claims.claim: The repository EditorConfig declares the lookup root, so a conforming consumer resolving settings for this tree must not inherit settings from ancestor .editorconfig files above it.
claims.trigger: Resolving EditorConfig settings for files under this repository root
claims.exceptions: Does not prohibit descendant EditorConfig overrides; applies only to consumers honoring EditorConfig root semantics.
claims.enforcement_effect: Configuration lookup boundary; source directive verified, no runtime consumer executed.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Primary names the lookup boundary but assigns IMPLEMENTATION with no constraint IDs; replica calls it a root marker. This is preserved as reclassification, not claimed previously unseen text.
Quote contains root=true, but explanation/scenario concern concrete formatting values, Markdown whitespace and indentation; they do not express excluding inherited ancestor settings.

Following conventions and assigning explicit formatting values do not independently specify where lookup stops; an otherwise identical file with root=false satisfies those claims while inheriting unassigned ancestor properties.

claims.comparison_reason: An effective resolution boundary was described but dismissed as implementation in both Claude coverage ledgers and not represented as a constraint; independent quote overlap does not establish semantic coverage. Candidate for adjudication, not proven EXTRA.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: Place an ancestor .editorconfig defining end_of_line=crlf for *.txt, leave this repository without an end_of_line assignment, and resolve a child text file with a conforming consumer. root=true excludes the ancestor assignment; root=false can inherit it while all explicitly recorded formatting values remain unchanged.
claims.adjudication_question: Should configuration-inheritance boundaries count as independently registered effective constraints? No runtime execution used.
